assessment.summary: A present, quantified toll of hundreds of thousands of conflict-related deaths a year across dozens of countries; overall fatalities eased slightly in 2025 but stayed higher than any other year since 2018, while the number of interstate conflicts doubled. Civilian harm in the largest of those wars has kept rising through 2026, with Ukraine's January-August civilian casualties 55% above the same period in 2025.
assessment.timeframe: Chronic and ongoing, with conflict-related fatalities near a multi-year high, interstate armed conflict having doubled in 2025, and civilian casualties in Ukraine climbing through 2026.

claims.text: The overall estimated number of conflict-related fatalities reduced slightly, by 4.2 per cent, from 249,000 in 2024 to 238,000 in 2025 — still higher than any other year in the period 2018-25 (SIPRI Yearbook 2026).

There were five major armed conflicts in 2025 (involving over 10,000 conflict-related fatalities each), one more than in 2024, while the number of high-intensity conflicts (1,000-9,999 fatalities) fell from 23 in 2024 to 20 in 2025 (SIPRI Yearbook 2026).

The number of interstate armed conflicts doubled from three in 2024 to six in 2025, involving at least 13 states, while the number of states with armed conflict on their territory fell slightly from 50 in 2024 to 49 in 2025 (SIPRI Yearbook 2026).

Civilian casualties in Ukraine from January to August 2026 (2,222 killed; 13,058 injured) were 55 per cent higher than in the same period in 2025 and more than double the same period in 2024; at least 372 civilians were killed and 2,349 injured in August 2026 alone, the second highest monthly figure of the year after July (448 killed; 2,675 injured) (OHCHR Protection of Civilians in Armed Conflict - August 2026, published 16 September 2026).

description: Ongoing state-based and civil wars that already kill hundreds of thousands of people a year and displace tens of millions more. Conflict-related fatalities eased slightly in 2025 but stayed above every other year since 2018, while the number of interstate armed conflicts doubled to six, involving at least 13 states. Ukraine, the largest interstate war among them, has intensified further: more civilians were killed and injured there in the first eight months of 2026 than in the whole of 2025, with long-range missile and drone attacks the leading cause. Escalation, spillover between neighbouring conflicts, and breakdown of humanitarian norms are the primary pathways to wider regional or global instability.
name: Global Armed Conflict
